principles: Proof must remain sequential even when implementation can be parallel.
Layer 2 claims must be limited to tested Engineering project classes.
Expected blocks are valid only when they are explicitly part of the baseline contract and evidenced.
Local diagnostics and host transcripts are audit context, not capability proof.
drivers: The user needs a concrete execution document for formally unlocking Engineering Baseline.
The document must prevent false capability claims and framework bloat.
The plan must be usable by future agents without inventing missing gates.
Risky migration/security baselines need explicit block-or-gated-pass semantics.

options.name: A: Tighten the existing unlock plan
pros: Reuses the existing root document and avoids duplicate sources of truth.
Keeps the work focused on correctness and execution clarity.
Can align directly with the B-c886 contract changes already implemented.
cons: Requires careful editing so the document remains concise and does not become a second full baseline spec.

options.name: B: Create a separate new runbook document
pros: Could separate conceptual baseline spec from execution steps.
cons: Adds another document to keep synchronized.
Increases the risk of conflicting claim boundaries and arbitrary structure.
Does not fix a real correctness issue because an unlock execution plan file already exists.

options.name: C: Expand the Engineering baseline document itself
pros: Would keep all Layer 2 material in one document.
cons: Would blur baseline definition with formal unlock procedure.
Could make the baseline spec more cumbersome without improving proof correctness.

chosen: A: Tighten the existing unlock plan
rationale: Choose the existing unlock execution plan because the user asked for an execution document based on the Layer 2 unlock statement, and a root execution-plan file already exists. Updating that file avoids duplicate truth sources while allowing us to make the runbook concrete and claim-safe.

preMortem.scenario: The document accidentally claims production-grade unattended development from Engineering evidence.
preMortem.trigger: Allowed wording mentions production, unattended operation, or Authority-style completion without lower-layer proof.
preMortem.consequence: Future agents may overclaim Lattice capability and bypass Loop or Production Safety baselines.
preMortem.mitigation: Add explicit non-claims, final decision mapping, and higher-layer locked target checks.

preMortem.scenario: Risky migration or security baselines are treated as ordinary PASS work.
preMortem.trigger: ENG-DATA-MIGRATION-1 or ENG-AUTH-SECURITY-1 lacks refusal evidence, gate evidence, or expected-block semantics.
preMortem.consequence: A dangerous or impossible task could be reported as DONE without safety proof.
preMortem.mitigation: Require expected-block evidence or digest-backed gated PASS evidence and list missing gates as fail-closed blockers.

preMortem.scenario: The runbook becomes another broad framework layer instead of an execution document.
preMortem.trigger: The edit introduces new capability names, new layers, or optimization-focused process beyond the requested Layer 2 unlock.
preMortem.consequence: Lattice becomes more complex without a correctness gain.
preMortem.mitigation: Keep the file scoped to Engineering unlock execution, reference existing baseline and parallel development docs, and avoid adding new claims.
